messages.subject: an interesting example of facets
parts:
I'd like to point to an interesting example using facets and ask how
one might do something similar in ggplot2.

The example is from Charles Franklin at pollster.com who does a lot of
interesting charts (using R). See http://www.pollster.com/blogs/unemployment_trends_in_the_sta.php

He's showing unemployment rates for each of the states so he is really
pushing hard to use limited space as effectively as possible. I like
the fact that he used the spots in the facet grid for something other
than one of the small multiples. In one he puts a scale (so he can
avoid taking the space elsewhere) and in another he has information
about the source of the data.

I can imagine how one might do this in lattice, short of using grid
graphics to manually assemble the facets one by one, I don't know how
one would do it in ggplot2. Or maybe it's straightforward to get the
matrix of grid objects that make up the facets in a ggplot2 facet
grid.

Please don't take this as a criticism of ggplot2. I rely on it very
much and I am just thinking about how to use it to flatter Charles
Franklin by trying to imitate him.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: an interesting example of facets
parts:
Hi,

You might be able to get something fairly close by arranging different
plots with Grid viewports (example below). It would probably make more
sense to use facet_wrap and then modify particular panels as you
suggest, but I don't know how.

library(ggplot2)

str(diamonds)
# smaller dataset
dsmall <- subset(diamonds, color=="D")
dsmall$cut <- factor(dsmall$cut)

bycut <- function(f="Fair", geom=c("path", "smooth"), title=f){
## plot a subset
d <- subset(dsmall, cut %in% f)
d <- d[order(d$price), ]
p <- qplot(price, carat, data=d, geom=geom)+
opts(keep=c("panels", "title"), title=title,
plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "lines")) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(5000, 15000, by=5000), labels="") +
scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0, 3, by=1), labels="")

p
}

## loop over cut levels
all.plots <- llply(levels(diamonds$cut), bycut)

library(ggExtra) # r-forge
library(RGraphics) # CRAN

string <- "
A dataset containing the prices and other attributes of almost 54,000 diamonds

price: price in US dollars ($326–$18,823)\n
carat: weight of the diamond (0.2--5.01)
"
## this function splits the text to fit in a given viewport
g1 <- splitTextGrob(string)

## this is the blank plot showing the scales
g2 <- bycut(geom="blank", title="")
## now the bottom right marginal plot for all cut levels
g3 <- bycut(levels(dsmall$cut), title="all")

## combine all the grobs in a list
all.grobs <- c(all.plots, list(g1), list(g2), list(g3), ncol=4)

grid.newpage()
## arrange is just a wrapper around grid.layout etc.
do.call(arrange, all.grobs)


I couldn't get the empty plot to show the scales nicely (and for some
reason the tick marks have different positions), and the text grob
could use some fine tuning.

Best,

baptiste
